measured_by: un_deltaXX, lane proofbundle, at head 7bdfb31 plus the R8 fix
why_this_file_exists: The scanner in tests/test_membership_hashable_guard.py gained a second detector on 2026-09-14: it now measures the CONSTRUCTION of a hash container from parsed data, not only the membership test. The first sharp run found seven pre-existing sites. They are carried by name so the gate can be sharp for anything NEW without blocking every landing on day one. This is a NAMED GAP, not permission: each entry still has to be closed.
why_the_detector_was_missing: The older detector visits ast.Compare with in/not in and requires the container to be a MODULE-LEVEL name. Both conditions missed cap1.py:220, where the container is built locally and the hashing happens inside the comprehension. Measured: zero hits against the full source of cap1.py while the defect was executably reproducible. A scanner that knows a class in only one of its shapes reports green and means 'this shape is not measured'.
honest_limit: The detector matches the .get(...) idiom only. A subscript on genuinely foreign data (doc['x']) escapes it, and so does a value bound to a variable first. Narrowing to .get was itself measured: including subscripts produced a false positive at relation_statement.py:340, where the list is built in-house a few lines above. Contract: test_UNTERGRENZE_ein_index_auf_fremde_daten_entgeht_dem_detektor.

carried.exposure: attacker-supplied: the predicate under validation. A list-valued 'assurance' raises TypeError inside the comprehension.
NICHT GEMESSEN. Note: str(...) makes the value hashable, so this one may be safe by construction — to be judged, not assumed.
operator-configured (allowed_issuers from the policy dict), not attacker-supplied; a partial guard _pinned_key_forgeable already runs on the same value. Lower severity than the agent_review sites.

matching: AN ENTRY IS MATCHED BY (file, qualname, expr) AND BY COUNT, NEVER BY LINE NUMBER. Two measurements drove this shape, in this order. FIRST, 2026-09-15: merging origin/main added 19 lines to agent_review.py, all seven carried sites moved, and a baseline bound to file:line reported its own seven entries as NEW — a line number is a property of the surrounding file, not of the site. SECOND, the same day, an adversarial lens falsified the first repair: keyed on (file, expr) alone, closing the carried attacker-exposed site in derive_limitation_codes and opening a brand-new unguarded construction with the SAME expression elsewhere in the same file kept the count at three and the guard stayed green — measured, with a real TypeError: unhashable type: 'list' in the new code. The old line-bound rule WOULD have caught it. qualname closes that: a new site lands in a different enclosing definition, so its key is not carried. last_seen_line is informational, for navigation only, and is allowed to drift.
